newsitem.title: USA: Triarc to spin off beverage, restaurant units.
newsitem.headline: Triarc to spin off beverage, restaurant units.

text.p: Triarc Cos Inc. said Tuesday it plans to spin off its Royal Crown and Mistic beverage units and Arby's restaurant business to Triarc shareholders and will instead focus on its liquefied petroleum and speciality chemicals businesses.
Under the plan, the company will offer up to 20 percent of its the beverage and restaurant businesses to the public and spin off the remainder of the shares to Triarc stockholders.
Triarc owns Arby's restaurants, Royal Crown Co. and Mistic Brands soft drinks, dyes and speciality chemicals company C.H. Patrick and liquefied petroleum gas company National Propane.
The offering and spinoff are not expected before the end of 1997's second quarter.
Triarc also said it established the Triarc Beverage Group, which will oversee the operations of Royal Crown and Mistic Brands.

Michael F. Weinstein, chief executive officer of Mistic, will become chief executive of the Triarc Beverage Group. John Carson, president of Royal Crown, will become chairman of the group, which will be based in White Plains, N.Y.

After the spinoff, Triarc Cos. will consist of National Propane Corp., in its capacity as the managing general partner, with about a 44 percent interest in National Propane Partners LP and C.H. Patrick.
Triarc said it will also have about $200 million in cash that will be available for future acquisitions and investments.
It said the new consumer products company will comprise the Triarc Restaurant Group -- Arby's Inc., p.t. Noodle's, T.J. Cinnamons and ZuZu -- and the beverage group.
Triarc said the company would like to expand its restaurant and beverage businesses by developing its existing brands and acquiring and developing additional product lines.
It said it believes "that the ability to raise the capital needed to fund this expansion will be significantly enhanced by having our beverage and restaurant businesses separate from Triarc."
Triarc stock was off 62.5 cents at $11.75 in midday trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
